bib.title: ThinK: Thinner Key Cache by Query-Driven Pruning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: ThinK: Thinner Key Cache by Query-Driven Pruning. Yuhui Xu, Zhanming Jie, Hanze Dong, Lei Wang, Xudong Lu, Aojun Zhou, Amrita Saha, Caiming Xiong, Doyen Sahoo (Salesforce AI Research; CUHK). ICLR 2025 conference paper (arXiv:2407.21018v3, 27 Feb 2025). Code: github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/ThinK.

COVERAGE: All 19 pages read, 79,835 chars (main text, Tables 1-12, appendices A-G, references skimmed). Figures 1-7 are image plots, so only captions were extracted; the plot data was not read. I did not run figures.py. Some table cells were truncated in extraction (the end of Table 7, row H2O/ThinK 822.4).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: ThinK prunes channels of the key cache (the D dimension, which other methods ignore), choosing channels per head by a query-driven score. Pruning 40% of key channels cuts total KV memory by 20% and keeps or improves LongBench accuracy when stacked on H2O or SnapKV.
  number: lambda=0.4 prunes 40% of key channels, giving a 20% total KV reduction
  setup: LongBench, LLaMA-3-8B/70B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, KV-size 128-2048, on top of H2O/SnapKV, A100 GPUs
  quote: "The pruning ratio of λ = 0.4 indicate that 40% of key cache channels are removed ,resulting in a 20% reduction in the total KV cache memory footprint."
  where: Sec 4.2, p7
- claim: Combined with KIVI quantization, ThinK reaches 2.8x peak memory reduction and raises the batch size from 4x (KIVI alone) to 5x relative to the FP16 baseline on one GPU.
  number: 2.8x peak memory, 5x batch
  setup: LLaMA-2-7B-chat, synthetic workload with prompt length 160 and output length 338, ThinK(0.4)
  quote: "THIN K integrated with KIVI can achieve 2.8× peak memory reduction while maintaining nearly the same quality, enabling a batch size increase from 4× (with KIVI alone) to 5× when using a single GPU."
  where: Abstract p1; Sec 4.4 p8
- claim: Query-driven scoring beats plain l1/l2 magnitude pruning at 40%. Magnitude pruning holds at 30% but degrades at 40%, worst for l1.
  number: SnapKV baseline avg 40.10; +l2 (0.3) 40.28; +l1 (0.4) 39.15; +l2 (0.4) 39.74. ThinK(0.4) on SnapKV 512 gets 40.55 (Table 2).
  setup: LLaMA-3-8B, LongBench, KV length 512, H2O and SnapKV
  quote: "A 30% pruning ratio can maintain accuracy; however, increasing it to 40% results in significant performance degradation, especially for l1 norm based pruning."
  where: Sec 3.1, Table 1, p4
- claim: The score is the Frobenius norm of the per-channel query-key outer product, computed over a recent observation window of the queries. Channels are chosen greedily to minimise the loss in attention weights.
  number: T = floor((1-λ)D) channels kept per head
  setup: method definition; the window follows SnapKV (Sobs = 32)
  quote: "Score i[j] = ∥Qi[:, j]Ki[:, j]T ∥F , I i = TopT (Scorei, T)."
  where: Sec 3.2, p4
- claim: At equal memory, ThinK beats eviction-only baselines, so it spends the memory better.
  number: Mistral-7B, SnapKV avg at 54.5 M: vanilla 34.52 vs ThinK 35.16. At 822.5 M: 41.97 vs 42.27. H2O at 208 M: 36.89 vs 37.49.
  setup: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, LongBench, vanilla KV-size shrunk to match memory (H2O 128 becomes 109)
  quote: "H2O or SnapKV combined with T HIN K consistently outperforms their counterparts without T HIN K while maintaining the same memory footprint."
  where: Table 7 and Fig 3a, p8-9
- claim: ThinK(0.4) at KV-size 2048 matches or exceeds the full-cache model on LLaMA-3-8B.
  number: SnapKV+ThinK(0.4) 41.91 vs full cache 41.86
  setup: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, LongBench
  quote: "Notably, with a KV-size of 2048 and a pruning ratio of 0.4, our method even surpasses the performance of LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct with a full KV cache."
  where: Sec 4.2, p7 (Table 2)
- claim: Applied to the full, uncompressed cache, pruning 40% to 50% of key channels does not hurt.
  number: LLaMA-3-8B avg 41.86 vanilla vs 42.27 (0.4), 42.25 (0.5), 41.43 (0.6). Mistral 42.71 vs 42.76, 42.53, 42.16.
  setup: LongBench, full KV, Table 9
  quote: "The results, as shown in Table 9, demonstrate that our method maintains superior performance even after pruning 40% of the key cache channels."
  where: App E, p16-17
- claim: Higher ratios hurt at small KV-sizes. λ=0.4 matches or beats SnapKV on Needle-in-a-Haystack, while λ>=0.5 drops at KV-size 128 and 512.
  number: LLaMA3-8B KV128: SnapKV 79.6, +ThinK(0.4) 79.6, +ThinK(0.5) 77.4. Mistral KV128: 77.8, 78.6 (0.4), 78.1 (0.5), 75.9 (0.6).
  setup: Needle-in-a-Haystack, SnapKV base, KV-size 128-2048
  quote: "However, when the pruning ratio increases to λ ≥ 0.5, we observe a drop in accuracy with smaller KV-sizes, particularly for 128 and 512, across both LLaMA-3 and Mistral models."
  where: Sec 4.3, Table 5, p7-8
- claim: Speed and throughput. Memory falls and TPOT improves, but TTFT rises because channel scores are computed during prefill.
  number: Memory 61.7 GB to 53.3 GB (0.4) and 51.2 GB (0.5). TTFT 7.0 to 10.4 ms. TPOT 0.27 to 0.25 ms/token. Throughput 5168 to 5518 tokens/s (0.4), 5676 (0.5). KIVI(4/4) 5168 vs vanilla 2557.
  setup: LLaMA-2-7B, batch 300, prompt 160, output 338, KIVI(4/4) base, KIVI methodology
  quote: "THIN K (40% pruning) improves the throughput of KIVI from 5168 tokens/s to 5518 tokens/s."
  where: App F, Tables 10-11, p17
- claim: Compared with SVD-based compression, ThinK loses much less accuracy at the same rate. This is an offline-vs-online contrast, and no reconstruction is needed.
  number: Palu -1.28% vs ThinK ~0; ASVD -5.21% vs ThinK -0.12%. Table 12 avg: Mistral vanilla 42.71, Palu 41.43, ThinK(0.4) 42.76. LLaMA-2-7B vanilla 33.37, ASVD 28.16, ThinK 33.25.
  setup: LongBench; Mistral-7B-v0.2 vs Palu at 80% compression; LLaMA-2-7B-Chat vs ASVD
  quote: "Our method demonstrates significantly better performance, with only a 0.12% performance drop compared to the 5.21% drop observed for ASVD."
  where: App G, Table 12, p17-18
- claim: Value-cache channels are harder to prune. Key magnitudes are very uneven across channels, while value magnitudes are uniform. Pruning 30% of both on LLaMA-3-8B stays acceptable.
  number: Table 8: LLaMA-3-8B KV-2048 SnapKV 41.58 vs ThinKV(0.3+0.3) 41.41. Mistral KV-512 SnapKV 40.46 vs (0.3+0.3) 39.80 vs (0.3+0.1) 40.29.
  setup: LongBench, H2O/SnapKV base
  quote: "pruning the Value cache channels is harder than pruning the Key cache channels. However, pruning 30% of both the Key cache and Value cache on LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct still results in acceptable performance."
  where: App D, p14-15
- claim: Observations motivating the method. The attention matrix is low-rank (the top 50 singular values carry over 90% of the energy). The key cache has a few high-magnitude channels.
  number: top-50 singular values > 90% of the energy
  setup: SVD of softmax(QK^T/sqrt(D)) in LLaMA-2-7B; layers 14 and 20 shown
  quote: "the normalized cumulative energy sum reveals that the top50 singular values account for over 90% of the total energy."
  where: Sec 2, p3
- claim: Keeping 32 recent tokens unpruned matters. Zero recent tokens costs accuracy; 128 gives no further gain.
  number: SnapKV+ThinK(0.4) avg 40.76 (0), 42.27 (32), 42.24 (128); H2O+ThinK 38.91, 40.47, 40.51
  setup: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, LongBench
  quote: "suggesting that retaining the most recent 32 KVs is sufficient to maintain optimal performance."
  where: Sec 4.4, Table 6, p8
- claim: KV cache sizing example. KV cache size is 2*B*S*L*N*D.
  number: 13 GB at context 2048 and batch 13, about equal to the weights
  setup: LLaMA-2-7B (MHA)
  quote: "a context length of 2048 and a batch size of 13 require storing a 13 GB KV cache, which is equivalent to the size of the model parameters."
  where: Sec 3.1, p3

LIMITS
- The authors concede that "our method slightly increases TTFT (Time-to-First-Token) due to channel importance computation" and that value-cache pruning "remains an open direction for future work."
- Evaluation is on LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack only. Models are LLaMA-2/3 and Mistral-7B, so GQA and MHA architectures are covered, but there are no newer models. Everything runs on A100.
- Throughput and memory results come from synthetic short workloads (prompt 160, output 338) on LLaMA-2-7B, not long-context serving.
- The 20% saving applies to the key half only, so total KV memory falls by λ/2.
- High λ (>=0.5) hurts at small KV-sizes. Differences on LongBench are often small, under 1 point, with no variance or seeds reported.
- Mistral value pruning loses accuracy.
- The per-channel pruning needs a custom kernel path (split pruned and unpruned keys, mask on the query). The authors say they are still optimising the implementation, and no integration with paged serving is reported.

BUILDS ON
- Eviction: H2O (Zhang et al., 2024c); SnapKV (Li et al., 2024), whose observation window is used; StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., 2023b).
- Quantization: KIVI (Liu et al., 2024b), including per-channel key quantization and the benchmark methodology; KVQuant (Hooper et al., 2024).
- Low-rank/SVD observations: Bhojanapalli et al. (2021); Loki (Singhania et al., 2024); Palu, ASVD and Eigen Attention as comparisons.
- Also cited: PyramidKV, FastGen, FlashAttention-2 (Dao, 2023), PagedAttention (Kwon et al., 2023).
- Benchmarks: LongBench (Bai et al., 2023); Needle in a Haystack (Kamradt, 2023).

CODE: None in the paper. Pseudo-formulas only:
- Eq 2: min_S ||Q_i K_i^T − Q_i S K_i^T||_F subject to trace(S)=floor((1-λ)D)
- Score_i[j] = ||Q_i[:,j] K_i[:,j]^T||_F, restricted to the last Sobs queries.
- Value score: ||softmax(Q_i[-Sobs:] K_i^T/√D) V_i[:, j]||_F

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p2): per-head channel mask. Scores per channel, keep the top T of D, store the binary mask with the pruned keys. Fastest way to see the method.
- Fig 2 (p5): decoding path. The query is pruned by the mask, and the pruned key multiplies the pruned query. The recent and new unpruned keys use the full query. The two products are concatenated.
- Fig 3 (p9): (a) LongBench score vs KV memory for H2O/SnapKV with and without ThinK; (b) peak memory vs batch size for vanilla, KIVI 4/4 and 2/2, with and without ThinK.
- Fig 4 (p12): key vs value channel magnitudes, LLaMA-2-7B layers 14 and 20. Keys have outlier channels and values are uniform.
- Fig 5 (p12): singular value energy and cumulative energy.
- Fig 6 (p13): Needle-in-a-Haystack heatmaps, Mistral.
- Fig 7 (p14): ThinK + KIVI pipeline (prune, then quantize by channel for keys and by token for values).

PROBLEMS: Figure content is not readable from the text extraction; table columns are jammed, but values are intact. The PDF contained no embedded instructions. The table 4 PCount column for KIVI shows 4.00 and PRe shows 8.00 (a very low synthetic score, from the source) so treat KIVI 2/2 numbers with care. A Table 7 row is truncated at one cell.
